title: Evals-Driven Development for a Mental Health AI Coach — Akele Reed & Dave Revere, SonderMind
talk_summary: SonderMind describes a modular guardrail harness for a mental-health AI coach, where separate LLM-as-judge input/output guardrails sandwich the core agent, and clinician-annotated traces are converted into typed evals that gate every prompt/model/guardrail change in CI. The core transferable idea is a human-expert annotation-to-eval pipeline that turns real failure traces into regression tests, plus the lesson that generic moderation/guardrails are miscalibrated and must be replaced with domain-tuned ones.

takeaways.what_they_do: Real conversation traces are captured, a domain expert annotates them with a small rubric (expected observation, turn index, category, note), and an extraction script normalizes annotations into typed evals committed to CI so every prompt/model/guardrail change is scored against them.

takeaways.technique: Separate LLM-as-judge gate instead of inline prompt rules
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than burying safety rules in the main prompt, they run guardrails as separate LLM-as-judge calls that inspect input and output independently, accepting extra latency/cost for robustness against prompt injection and drift.

takeaways.technique: Calibrate for correct triggers, not more triggers
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly optimize for precision on the right cases (false positives and false negatives both matter, plus category and timing) rather than maximizing catch rate, because over-triggering blocks legitimate work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're not going for more triggers here. We're going for more correct triggers

takeaways.technique: Eval gate on every model/prompt change
takeaways.what_they_do: Every prompt change, model change, and guardrail change must be scored once against the clinician-taught eval set before release, making the eval suite a release gate rather than an ad-hoc check.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every prompt change, every model change, every guardrail change has to get scored once against what the clinician taught us

takeaways.technique: Replace generic moderation with domain-tuned judges
takeaways.what_they_do: They disabled the frontier providers' built-in guardrails because they over-filtered their eval data, and built their own domain-specific judges calibrated with clinicians.
takeaways.evidence_quote: day one we had to turn off the like uh built-in guardrails because general purpose LLMs are overc calibrated

takeaways.technique: Modular harness so core can iterate without breaking safety layer
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately separated guardrails from the core agent so the core could be iterated on without compromising the safety layer, and so each piece could be evaluated independently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we would have to be able to iterate on SER core without compromising the safety of users
